analysis: The code flow: if state != RUNNING, either throw IllegalStateException (runtime) or set backup and call backup.deliver(packet). The latter may throw runtime exceptions but they propagate out, which is acceptable. In the else branch (state == RUNNING), a try-catch catches Exception from the I/O and serialization block. After that block, if errorDelivering is true, close() and backupDeliverer.deliver(packet) are called; if false, session.incrementServerPacketCount() is called. The post-try statements are unprotected: backupDeliverer may be null (NullPointerException), close() may throw runtime exceptions, and session.incrementServerPacketCount() could throw runtime exceptions. These unhandled runtime exceptions could disrupt execution.
